# `get_batch_stack_setting`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Return the configured batch stacking input files, pruning entries that no longer exist.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build established) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb7270, GetFileList @0x3a8b90, FormatFileList @0x3a7010 (64-bit build) |

Walks the selected input list under a mutex, checks the cached file metadata, refreshes it with filesystem queries and returns the surviving entries. Inaccessible entries or entries whose path no longer matches are erased from the stored list, so this getter changes the user-visible list (graded MUTATOR, tier C). In the 64-bit build the type key chooses between the star-trail list and the shared deepsky/comet list (firmware 9.75 has three separate lists, and the reply adds key_frame for deepsky and comet, or batch_startrails_mode for startrail); the 32-bit build ignores params and uses its single input list. Filesystem queries and the lock can block with no timeout.

Side effects: Refreshes the cached metadata of the batch input list and removes inaccessible or mismatched entries from it.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_batch_stack_setting"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional parameters. In the 64-bit build only the type key is read; absent, null, array, scalar or any other non-object params default to 0, as does a bad type. Other keys are ignored. The 32-bit build reads no params. The app also serialises a files member here, which the device does not read. [READ] |
| `params.type` | string | no | deepsky | Which input list to return: deepsky, startrail or comet (case-sensitive, exact). startrail selects the star-trail list; in firmware 9.31 deepsky and comet share the same list; in firmware 9.75 each of the three types has its own list and persisted file. A non-string or unknown value silently selects deepsky. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

No handler-specific error is reachable.

## Example

Request, query:

```json
{"id":161,"method":"get_batch_stack_setting"}
```

Request, query-startrail:

```json
{"id":162,"method":"get_batch_stack_setting","params":{"type":"startrail"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_batch_stack_setting","result":{"files":[{"name":"Example_target/frame_0001.fit","date":"2026-01-31 21:04:05","thn":"Example_target/frame_0001_thn.jpg","type":0}]},"code":0,"id":161}
```

Reply, ok-empty:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_batch_stack_setting","result":{"files":[]},"code":0,"id":163}
```
